title: Triage review of c28's kernel-drive ringswim on fresh seed 24 (labkit only): with the label-free drive at mu 0.75, kd 0.08, cells from noise divide on a near-clean tree (122 persistent splits, generation 8, merge/split 0.026), the L ring sits below the gate (1.37) as reported, and travel is short (max 3.5 BL in labkit)
summary: I ran the claim world with WORLD_P drive=kernel, mu=0.75, kd=0.08 on fresh seed 24 (labkit, 256^2, t=10000). From noise over the whole domain a bounded population forms (89 cells at the end, occupancy 0.20). It divides on an almost merge-free genealogy: 459 splits, 122 persistent, 12 merges, merge/split 0.026, max generation 8. 187 tracks move >= 1 body length, with labkit max 3.5. The link ring is in the right place but weak: L rim/core 1.37, rim/outside 7.93, membrane-like in 189/430 individuals, matching the finding's 1.36-1.38. This also explains my earlier control (20261025T2220-c24-review-ringswim-sibmd): with the kernel drive at the default mu=1.5, kd=0.03 division fell into fission-fusion, and lowering mu and raising kd restores clean division. I started c28's ringtrack for swimming lineages but stopped it at my session deadline before it finished, so the swim-ring-divide lineage count is not checked.

observations.finding: pack/seed24/FACTS.md: persistent splits 122, max generation 8, merges 12 (merge/split 0.026); L rim/core 1.37; 187 tracks >= 1 BL, max 3.5 BL

seeds_run.result: pass for division on a clean tree and the weak ring; swimming lineages not checked (ringtrack stopped)

verdicts.limitation: Triage only: one fresh seed and labkit only, so I did not check the finding's 82-90 tracks >= 3 BL or its 5-11 ringed swim-divide lineages, and I did not run chi=0. labkit's motion line (max 3.5 BL over t=10000) shows the swimming is slow compared with the label drive.
